$\frac{1}{2}\left[a_1\left(b_2-b_3\right)+a_2\left(b_3-b_1\right)+a_3\left(b_1-b_2\right)\right]=0\begin{array}{cc}\Rightarrow & 1\left(3-\frac{a}{3}\right)-2\left(\frac{a}{3}-1\right)+\alpha(1-3)=0 \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{9-a}{3}-2\left(\frac{a-3}{3}\right)+0=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 9-a-2 a+6=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 3 a=15 \\ \Rightarrow & a=5\end{array}$

$\begin{array}{rlrl}&\Rightarrow |i+z| =|i-z| \\ & \Rightarrow x^2+(1+y)^2 =x^2+(1-y)^2 \\ &\Rightarrow x^2+y^2+2 y+1 =x^2+y^2+1-2 y \\ &\Rightarrow 4 y =0 \\ &\Rightarrow y =0\end{array}$ ie, $x$-axis.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $z=x+i y, z^{1 / 3}=a-i b$, then $\frac{x}{a}-\frac{y}{b}=k\left(a^2-b^2\right)$, where $k$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { Here, } z^{1 / 3}=a-i b \\ & \Rightarrow z=(a-i b)^3 \\ & \Rightarrow z=a^3-3 a^2(i b)+3 a(i b)^2-(i b)^3 \\ & \Rightarrow x+i y=\left(a^3-3 b^2 a\right)+i\left(-3 a^2 b+b^3\right) \end{aligned}$
Equating real and imaginary parts, we get $x=a\left(a^2-3 b^2\right) \text { and } y=b\left(b^2-3 a^2\right)$
Now, $\frac{a\left(a^2-3 b^2\right)}{a}-\frac{b\left(b^2-3 a^2\right)}{b}=k\left(a^2-b^2\right)\Rightarrow 4 a^2-4 b^2=k\left(a^2-b^2\right) \Rightarrow k=4$

Now, $|z+1|=\left|3 e^{i \theta}+1\right|\begin{aligned} & =|(3 \cos \theta+1)+(3 i \sin \theta)| \\ & =\sqrt{(3 \cos \theta+1)^2+(3 \sin \theta)^2}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\sqrt{9+1+6 \cos \theta} \\ & =\sqrt{10+6 \cos \theta}\end{aligned}\sin \theta, \cos \theta$ ranges from -1 to 1 , the maximum value of $|z+1|$ occur, when $\cos \theta=1$. Therefore, $\operatorname{Max}|z+1|=\sqrt{10+6}=\sqrt{16}=4$ For minimum value The minimum value of $z+1$ occures, when $z$ is at the centre of the circle $|z|=3$. In this case $z=0$. On putting $z=0$ into the expression, we have $\operatorname{Min}(|z+1|)=|0+1|=1$ Hence, maximum value of $|z+1|=4$ minimum value of $|z+1|=1$

questions.q: The locus of the point $z$ satisfying $\arg \left(\frac{z-1}{z+1}\right)=k$, (where $k$ is non-zero) is
options: a straight line making an angle $60^{\circ}$ with the $x$-axis
questions.solution:
We have, arg $\left(\frac{z-1}{z+1}\right)=k,(k \neq 0)$
Put $z=x+i y$, we get $\begin{array}{cc} & \arg \left(\frac{x-1+i y}{x+1+i y}\right)=k \\ \Rightarrow & \arg \left[\frac{(x-1+i y)(x+1-i y)}{(x+1+i y)(x+1-i y)}\right]=k \\ \Rightarrow & \arg \left[\frac{\left(x^2-1\right)+i y(2)+y^2}{(x+1)^2+y^2}\right]=k \\ \Rightarrow & \arg \left[\frac{x^2+y^2-1+2 i y}{(x+1)^2+y^2}\right]=k \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{2 y}{x^2+y^2-1}=k \\ \Rightarrow & {\left[\because \arg (z)=\tan ^{-1} \frac{y}{x}\right]} \\ \Rightarrow & \left(x^2+y^2\right) k-k-2 y=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad & k x^2+k y^2-2 y-k=0 \\ \Rightarrow & x^2+y^2-\frac{2 y}{k}-1=0 \end{array}$ \\ Which represent a circle of centre $(0,1 / k)$ i.e. on $y$-axis.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation $|z+i|-|z-i|=k$ represent a hyperbola, if
questions.solution:
Let $z=x+i y$, then $|z+i|-|z-i|=k$ becomes $\therefore  \sqrt{x^2+(y+1)^2}-\sqrt{x^2+(y-1)^2}=k...(i)$
or $x^2+(y+1)^2-x^2-(y-1)^2=k\left\{\sqrt{x^2+(y+1)^2}+\sqrt{x^2+(y-1)^2}\right\}\therefore \sqrt{x^2+(y-1)^2}+\sqrt{x^2+(y+1)^2}=\frac{4 y}{k}...(ii)$
From Eqs. (i) and (ii),
$2 \sqrt{x^2+(y+1)^2}=k+\frac{4 y}{k}\Rightarrow 4 x^2+4 y^2+8 y+4=k^2+\frac{16 y^2}{k^2}+8 y\Rightarrow  4 x^2+\left(4-\frac{16}{k^2}\right) y^2=k^2-4$
For an hyperbola, $\frac{4 k^2-16}{k^2} \lt 0 \Rightarrow k^2-4 \lt 0\Rightarrow |k| \lt 2$ or $-2 \lt k \lt 2$

questions.q: If $n_1, n_2$ are positive integers, then $(1+i)^{n_1}+\left(1+i^3\right)^{n_1}+\left(1+i^5\right)^{n_2}+\left(1+i^7\right)^{n_2}$ is a real number if and only if
options: $n_1, n_2$ are any two negative integers
$n_1, n_2$ are both any positive integers
questions.solution:
Expression can be written as $=(1+i)^{n_1}+(1-i)^{n_1}+(1+i)^{n_2}+(1-i)^{n_2}=2^{n_1 / 2}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+i \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{n_1}+2^{n_1 / 2}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-i \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{n_1}+2^{n_2 / 2}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+i \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{n_2}+2^{n_2 / 2}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-i \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{n_2}=2^{n_1 / 2}\left\{\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{4}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{n_1}+\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{4}-i \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{n_1}\right\}+2^{n_2 / 2}\left\{\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{4}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{n_2}+\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{4}-i \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{n_2}\right\}+2^{n_2 / 2}\left\{\cos \frac{n_2 \pi}{4}+i \sin \frac{n_2 \pi}{4}\right.\left.+\cos \frac{n_2 \pi}{4}-\sin \frac{n_2 \pi}{4}\right\}=2^{n_1 / 2} \cdot 2 \cos \frac{n_1 \pi}{4}+2^{n_2 / 2} \cdot 2 \cos \frac{n_2 \pi}{4}=\mathrm{real}$
ie, $n_1, n_2$ are any two positive integers.

questions.q: If $\left|\frac{z_1}{z_2}\right|=1$ and $\arg \left(z_1 z_2\right)=0$, then
questions.solution:
Let $z_1=\gamma_1\left(\cos \theta_1+i \sin \theta_1\right)$. Given that, $\left|\frac{z_1}{z_2}\right|=1\Rightarrow\left|q_1\right|=\left|z_2\right| \Rightarrow\left|z_1\right|=\left|z_2\right|=\gamma_1$
Now, $\arg \left(z_1 z_2\right)=0 \Rightarrow \arg \left(z_1\right)+\arg \left(z_2\right)=0\Rightarrow \quad \arg \left(z_2\right)=-\theta_1$
Therefore, $z_2=\gamma_1\left(\cos \left(-\theta_1\right)+i \sin \left(-\theta_1\right)\right.\begin{array}{cc} & =\gamma_1\left(\cos \theta_1-i \sin \theta_1\right)=\bar{z}_1 \\ \Rightarrow & \bar{z}_2=\left(\bar{z}_1\right)=z_1 \Rightarrow z_2 \bar{z}_2=z_1 z_2 \\ \Rightarrow & \left|z_2\right|^2=z_1 z_2 \end{array}$

questions.q: If $Q$ is real and $z_1, z_2$ are connected by $z_1^2+z_2^2+2 z_1 z_2 \cos \theta=0$, then triangle with vertices $0, z_1$ and $z_2$ is
questions.solution:
$z_1^2+z_2^2+2 z_1 z_2 \cos \theta=0\Rightarrow \quad\left(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\right)^2+2\left(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\right) \cos \theta+1=0\Rightarrow\left(\frac{z_1}{z_2}+\cos \theta\right)^2=-\left(1-\cos ^2 \theta\right)=-\sin ^2 \theta\Rightarrow \quad \frac{z_1}{z_2}=-\cos \theta \pm i \sin \theta\Rightarrow \quad\left|\frac{z_1}{z_2}\right|=\sqrt{(-\cos \theta)^2+(\sin \theta)^2}=1\begin{array}{lrl}\Rightarrow & \left|z_1\right|=\left|z_2\right| \\ \Rightarrow & \left|z_1-0\right|=\left|z_2-0\right|\end{array}$
Thus, triangle with vertices $0, z_1, z_2$ is iscosceles.

questions.q: If $\cos \alpha+\cos \beta+\cos \gamma=\sin \alpha+\sin \beta+\sin \gamma=0$, then the value of $\cos 3 \alpha+\cos 3 \beta+\cos 3 \gamma$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { Let } a=\cos \alpha+i \sin \alpha \\ & \qquad \begin{aligned} b & =\cos \beta+i \sin \beta \\ c & =\cos \gamma+i \sin \gamma\end{aligned}\end{aligned}$
then; $a+b+c=(\cos \alpha+\cos \beta+\cos \gamma)+i(\sin \alpha+\sin \beta+\sin \gamma)=0+i 0=0\Rightarrow a^3+b^3+c^3=3 a b c\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow(\cos 3 \alpha+i \sin 3 \alpha)+(\cos 3 \beta \\ &+i \sin 3 \beta) \\ &+(\cos 3 \gamma+i \sin 3 \gamma)\end{aligned}=3[\cos (\alpha+\beta+\gamma)+i \sin (\alpha+\beta+\gamma)]\Rightarrow \cos 3 \alpha+\cos 3 \beta+\cos 3 \gamma=3 \cos (\alpha+\beta+\gamma)$

questions.q: If $\mathbf{i} z^4+1=0$, then $z$ can take the value
questions.solution:
$i z^4=-1\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & z^4=-\frac{1}{i} \\ \Rightarrow & z^4=i \\ \Rightarrow & z=(i)^{1 / 4}=(0+i)^{1 / 4} \\ \Rightarrow & z=\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{2}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{2}\right)^{1 / 4} \\ \Rightarrow & z=\cos \frac{\pi}{8}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{8}\end{array}$
(using De Moirrels theorem)
